m3-rescope-guard-latch.title: rescope() bookend guard + retrofit path + one-way latch
m3-rescope-guard-latch.imperative: In rescope() (:3089), refuse when the target carries the bookend flag, BEFORE the field overwrite. Add 'bookend' to the overwritable tuple (:3099-3100) so rescope can SET the flag (retrofit path) on a gate that is not yet marked. Because the guard runs before the overwrite, once bookend is set, every later rescope of that gate (including one trying to set bookend:false) is refused -- a one-way latch. Write tests FIRST (RED): test_amend_rescope_refuses_bookend_gate, test_amend_rescope_sets_bookend_flag_via_overwritable, test_amend_rescope_bookend_flag_is_one_way_latch. Observe RED, implement to GREEN.

why_trail.why: Candidate B is chosen and specified: one _bookend_ceiling-style helper beside _floor(), guards in add/drop/rescope/retext-check, bookend added to rescope's overwritable tuple as the one-way-latch retrofit path. retext-check guard is a deliberate contested override per the handoff. Undeclared plans must behave identically to 9b38b9d9.

Implemented _is_bookend(tid) beside _floor(); add() computes a ceiling = max index of any bookend-marked gate and refuses insert_at > ceiling. Diverged from design-B's literal '+1' ceiling formula, which would NOT refuse appending immediately after a bookend that is the last item (off-by-one: ceiling=len(items) makes insert_at==ceiling==len(items) pass, exactly the append-past-archive case the design's own prose says must be refused). Using ceiling = bookend's own index (no +1) so insert_at>ceiling correctly refuses landing after it. Both required tests green.

drop() now refuses when _is_bookend(tid), checked before the pending-status check, regardless of status, with EngineError(task_id, verb='amend-drop', status). Reproduces and closes the measured gap: the probe's exact three-drop delta against the probe fixture is now refused and leaves the checklist unmutated. Backward compat holds: undeclared plans drop a pending closing gate exactly as at 9b38b9d9.

rescope() refuses _is_bookend(tid) before the field overwrite, regardless of status. Added 'bookend' to the overwritable tuple -- the retrofit path. Because the guard fires before the overwrite, once bookend=true lands, every later rescope on that gate (including bookend:false) is refused: a one-way latch, asserted explicitly by test_amend_rescope_bookend_flag_is_one_way_latch. Full Amend* test classes (44 tests) still green -- no regression to existing rescope behavior.

retext-check now refuses _is_bookend(tid) before the status check and before any mutation. This is the contested, deliberate override the handoff calls out: without it, retext-check could rewrite a frozen gate's command check to something trivially true and let it pass, defeating the drop/rescope guards while leaving the gate standing. The two sanctioned recovery paths (fix template + re-instantiate, or waive under recorded authority) stay open. Full Amend* suite: 45 passed, no regression.

Confirmed rather than changed: the new bookend guards raise before any of new_items/new_tasks are touched (guards run inline in the ops loop, commit only happens after the loop at :3177+), so the existing copy-then-commit discipline covers the new refusal paths for free. Test passed on first run, no engine change needed for this item.

spine_amend handler (:2404-2424) is confirmed a pure pass-through: writes the delta beside the bound spine and calls run_engine('amend', ...) -> checklist_engine.main() -> amend(), which raises the new bookend EngineErrors through the same as_result() path every existing amend refusal already uses. No schema/handler change needed or made; added one sentence to the tool description only, per the three independent design agents' shared conclusion.

Both required commands run in a fresh subprocess with SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION/SPINE_PARENT/CREW_SCRATCH_DIR unset, per #269. test_checklist_engine.py: 466 passed, 140 subtests passed. test_mcp_spine_server.py + test_mcp_identity.py: 62 passed, 14 subtests passed. No failures, no skips.
